text: The opening verses of Genesis present creation as the deliberate act of God, not an accident of matter. The narrative establishes order, purpose, and distinction by divine word.
source_title: Matthew Henry's Commentary on the Whole Bible
author: Matthew Henry

text: The Pulpit Commentary notes that the creation account frames Israel's worship by grounding all life and time in the Lord's sovereign initiative.
author: H.D.M. Spence and Joseph Exell

text: Easton's Bible Dictionary highlights that 'Eden' language in Genesis serves both geographic and theological purposes, marking the goodness of God's provision and fellowship.
author: M.G. Easton

text: The International Standard Bible Encyclopedia emphasizes that Genesis 1–2 supplies the foundational worldview for biblical theology: God as Creator, humanity as image-bearer, and creation as accountable to divine command.
author: ISBE Editorial Board

text: Jamieson-Fausset-Brown observes that each creative act is presented as both powerful and orderly, reinforcing God's authority over chaos and history.
author: Jamieson, Fausset, and Brown

text: John Gill's exposition underscores that divine speech in Genesis is effective and unfailing; what God commands comes to pass, revealing both sovereignty and wisdom.
source_title: John Gill's Exposition of the Bible
author: John Gill

text: Strong's lexical entries for creation terms note purposeful formation and ordering, supporting a theological reading centered on God's intentional design rather than randomness.
author: James Strong

text: Smith's Bible Dictionary presents the Sabbath pattern as a theological gift: rest ordered by God, not merely human cessation, shaping worship and trust.
author: William Smith
